questions.question: Distinguish between goods and services and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Goods are tangible, physical products that can be seen, touched and stored, e.g. bread, shoes, phones. Services are intangible activities performed for others, e.g. a haircut, a taxi ride, teaching, banking.

questions.question: Explain the difference between producers and consumers, and why most people are both.
questions.expected_answer: Producers make goods or provide services, usually to earn income; consumers buy and use goods and services to satisfy needs and wants. Most people are producers when they work and earn, and consumers when they spend their income.

questions.question: Trace a loaf of bread through primary, secondary and tertiary production.
questions.expected_answer: Primary: farmer grows wheat. Secondary: miller grinds wheat into flour; baker bakes bread. Tertiary: transport delivers bread; shop sells it to the consumer (with banking and insurance services). Value is added at each stage.
